slides.title: Two lines, one output
slides.text: Tally finds two lines in the Machine Hall. One adds 2 and then multiplies by 3. The other multiplies by 3 and then adds 6. Every box she sends through comes out the same from both.

slides.title: Equal for every input
slides.text: The first line is 3(x + 2) and the second is 3x + 6. They are equivalent expressions: the same value for every x. The 3 multiplies both parts of the sum, 3 times x and 3 times 2. That is the distributive property.

focus.cue: Each column is one input sent down both lines.
Both rows give 9 when x is 1.
The rows match in every column: 21 and 21 for x = 5.

slides.title: A few matches are not proof
slides.text: Now compare 2x with x². They match when x is 0 and when x is 2, so two tests could fool you. For x = 3 they give 6 and 9. Expressions are equivalent only when a rule shows they match for every number.

visual.label: Two lines that match only sometimes
head: x

focus.cue: For x = 3 the rows differ: 6 and 9.

slides.title: Factor: the same rule, backward
slides.text: Start with 4x + 12. Both terms are 4 times something: 4 × x and 4 × 3. Take the 4 outside and write 4(x + 3). To check, expand it again: 4 times x is 4x, and 4 × 3 = 12.
steps: 4 is a factor of both terms

slides.title: Like terms join, a sum leaves whole
slides.text: Terms with the same letter are like terms: 2x + 3x + 4 = 5x + 4, and the 4 stays apart. Taking away a sum takes away every term in it, so 8x − (3x + 2) = 5x − 2. A new form can show something new: x + 0.2x = 1.2x says that adding 20% is multiplying by 1.2.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for expressions that are equal.

words.means: expressions with the same value for every number, such as 3(x + 2) and 3x + 6
multiplying a sum multiplies each part: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6
terms with the same variable, such as 2x and 3x, which add to 5x
to write a sum as a product, such as 4x + 12 = 4(x + 3)

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Machine Line at Same Output. Decide if two lines always match, then rebuild a line another way and run both to check.
slides.alt: Machine Line on a phone: line A adds 2 and then multiplies by 3, line B multiplies by 3 and then adds 6, and three tiles ask if they always match.
